correctness.rationale: The unrestricted induction shows every depth-d truth function is a linear form in finitely many basis truth functions. Existential affine functional tests determine exactly the affine successor hull, including the empty case; the separating affine-functional lemma supplies the converse. An actual affine basis gives r+1 successor witnesses and rank proves the lower bound. An exhaustive finite 256-subset enumeration of the eight attained depth-one vectors yields 96 affine hulls, and an independently computed 32-affine-test table yields exactly the same classes; the resulting 192 count and sharp five-successor example are valid. Direct Kripke semantic evaluation on 12,288 rooted three-world cases agrees. Limitations of finite checking are explicitly separated from the general mathematical proof.

value.rationale: An exact finite-depth expressivity invariant for parity-only modal logic directly addresses an explicitly motivated basis-sensitive model-comparison problem. The one-variable 192-theory census is a natural first nontrivial nesting level (depth one has only eight types), and the five-successor sharp bound detects genuine expansion of branching requirements outside S5. These are complete semantic and optimality statements rather than arbitrary parameter substitutions; they supply concrete finite test cases for future fragment-specific bisimulation work.
